prompt: Return the most frequent character in a string; when counts tie, the character whose first occurrence comes earliest wins. Return '?' for an empty string.
explanation: Visiting characters in string order and skipping any position that is not a character's first occurrence (s.indexOf(c) != i) processes candidates in first-occurrence order. Combined with a strict > comparison on counts, the earliest candidate automatically survives ties. The inner loop recounts each candidate; a map of counts would also work if you record first positions for tie-breaking.
hints: Loop over positions i; the test s.indexOf(c) == i is true only at a character's first occurrence.
For each first occurrence, count how many times that character appears with a second loop.
Replace the champion only when count > bestCount; because candidates arrive in first-occurrence order, ties keep the earlier character.
